sections.s04.s0: The structure every real-time game shares, then media processing. Work items 1 to 5 in order in one small pygame sketch that you keep extending. Add items 6 to 8 to the same sketch once it has enough objects to be worth measuring. Do item 9, Pillow and ffmpeg, as a separate script.
sections.s04.s1: One small, complete game rather than a large unfinished one. Build the playable core with delta-time movement first, then the start, pause and game-over states, then levels and difficulty, then settings, and package last. Stop adding features once the core loop is fun.

s04.s0.0.how: Write a pygame window whose while loop has three clearly separated functions: handle events from pygame.event.get, update positions, then draw and call pygame.display.flip. Read the fixed versus variable timestep sections of the game loop chapter.
s04.s0.0.done: You can draw the loop from memory and say what goes wrong when drawing and updating are mixed together.

s04.s0.1.how: Get dt = clock.tick(fps) / 1000 from pygame.time.Clock and move a sprite by speed * dt. Run it at 30 and 144 FPS and time how long the sprite takes to cross the screen in each case.
s04.s0.1.done: The crossing time is the same, within a frame, at 30 and 144 FPS.

s04.s0.2.how: Load a sprite sheet once with pygame.image.load(...).convert_alpha(), cut frames with Surface.subsurface, and advance the frame index on a timer in a pygame.sprite.Sprite subclass. Draw a group of them with Group.draw.
s04.s0.2.done: An animated character plays at a set frame rate that does not change when the game FPS changes.

s04.s0.3.how: Detect hits with Rect.colliderect, then with a circle distance check, and use pygame.sprite.spritecollide for groups. Spawn 2,000 objects, time the all-pairs check, then add a uniform grid and time it again.
s04.s0.3.done: You have before and after timings showing the grid cuts collision time with 2,000 objects.

s04.s0.4.how: Define the states MENU, PLAYING, PAUSED and GAME_OVER with enum.Enum, give each its own handle, update and draw functions, and switch between them in one place. Add pause on Escape and check the game does not advance while paused.
s04.s0.4.done: The main loop has no if chains about state beyond one dispatch, and pausing freezes all movement.

s04.s0.5.how: Read the Component chapter, then write the same enemy two ways: one class with position, health and render code, and an entity holding separate component objects. Note how many lines each needs for a second enemy type.
s04.s0.5.done: You can say for your own game whether plain classes are enough, with a reason based on how many entity types it has.

s04.s0.6.how: Load every pygame.mixer.Sound and image once at start-up into a dict keyed by name, and play background music with pygame.mixer.music. Add a print in the loader to confirm no file is loaded twice during play.
s04.s0.6.done: Sounds play without a stall on first use, and the loader runs once per asset.

s04.s0.7.how: Run the game under python -m cProfile -s cumtime for 30 seconds and find the top three functions. Also time update and draw each frame with time.perf_counter, print the worst frame, and fix the largest cost.
s04.s0.7.done: You have a measured worst-case frame time below 16 ms under normal play, with before and after numbers.

s04.s0.8.how: With Pillow, open an image, resize it, crop it and save it as a thumbnail. Then call ffmpeg through subprocess.run with an argument list to extract audio from a video file, and check the return code.
s04.s0.8.done: One script creates thumbnails for a folder of images and another extracts an audio track, both raising on failure.

s04.s1.0.how: Choose a small genre such as a shooter, a platformer or a puzzle game, write its rules on one page, and build the core loop first. Add the start screen, score display and game-over screen using the state machine from the Learn section.
s04.s1.0.done: Someone else can start the game, play, lose, see their score and start again without help.

s04.s1.1.how: Pass dt in seconds from Clock.tick into every update function, and express all speeds and timers in units per second. Cap dt at a maximum so a stall does not move objects through walls.
s04.s1.1.done: The game plays the same with the frame rate capped at 30 and at 120 FPS.

s04.s1.2.how: Store level layouts or difficulty parameters (spawn rate, enemy speed) in data such as a JSON file, not in code. Increase difficulty with score or time, then play from the start and record the point where you lose.
s04.s1.2.done: Difficulty changes during play, and adding a new level means editing data rather than code.

s04.s1.3.how: Add a settings screen that changes music and effect volume with set_volume and rebinds the movement keys. Save the choices to a JSON file and load it on start-up.
s04.s1.3.done: Changed volume and key bindings take effect immediately and are still set after a restart.

s04.s1.4.how: Load all assets through a path helper that handles sys._MEIPASS, build with PyInstaller including the assets folder, then run the result on a machine or VM that has no Python installed.
s04.s1.4.done: The packaged game starts with sound and images on a clean machine without Python.
